zh: 这本来是件好事，但袁世凯却怀着鬼胎，但亦无法，只好等纰漏出来以后再来想办法——终于有一天，为吴长庆办文案的幕僚。而且也教袁世凯读过书的周家禄，将他找了去有话问。『慰亭，』他问∶『你是中书科中书？』『怎么样？』袁世凯不置可否，先打听出了什么事。『你看！』是北洋来的公事，说庆军保奖一案，中书科中书袁世凯，保升同知，业已奉旨允准。惟本部遍查档册，中书科中书并无袁世凯其人；请饬该员申复云云。袁世凯一则以喜，一则以忧，喜的是平地起楼台，搞了个五品同知，这个职务是武职，故别称『司马』；但官却是文官，前程无量，比二、三品的副将、参将还值钱；忧的是资历上的中书科中书原是假冒的，这个底缺如果不存在，升同知的美梦也就落空了。心里七上八下，表面却很沉着，『周先生，』他笑嘻嘻地说∶『你倒猜上一猜。』『用不着猜，你当初拿来的那张捐官的「部照」，姓不错，是袁，名字不是，当然是借来的。』『是，是，周先生明见万里，这件事，』他打了个千说∶『请周先生成全。』『成全不用说，据实呈复，连庆公都要担个失察的处分。』周家禄紧接着说∶『现在有两个办法，一个容易，一个麻烦，要你自己挑。』『那请周先生指教，是怎么样的两个办法。』『先说容易的，你改用部照上的名字。』周家禄说∶『这个办法，不但容易，而且方便。你方便，只要一角公文，袁世凯为袁某某的改名。恢复原名即可。』袁世凯不愿用这个容易方便的法子，因为他在韩国已是知名人物；尤其有关系的是，朝中自慈禧太后、恭王到总理衙门章京，都知道有个在朝鲜立了功的袁世凯，一改名字，区区同知，有谁知道。
en: This ought to have been good news, but Yuan Shikai had a guilty secret. There was nothing he could do except wait for the flaw to emerge and then find a remedy. At last Zhou Jialu, a member of Wu Changqing’s secretariat who handled correspondence and had also taught Yuan, summoned him for a question. “Weiting, are you a secretary in the Secretariat Office?” “What is the matter?” Yuan neither confirmed nor denied it, first seeking to learn what had happened. “Look at this.” It was an official communication from Beiyang concerning the Qing Army’s recommendations for rewards. Yuan Shikai, secretary in the Secretariat Office, had received imperial approval for promotion to deputy prefect. But after searching its records, the ministry could find no secretary of that name. He was to be instructed to submit an explanation. Yuan felt both delight and anxiety. His delight was that he had built a tower from level ground and obtained a fifth-rank deputy prefecture. The post carried military duties—hence its other designation, “sima”—but its holder was a civil official with unlimited prospects, making it more valuable than a second- or third-rank military command. His anxiety was that the secretaryship in his record was fraudulent. If that underlying appointment did not exist, his dream of becoming deputy prefect would collapse. Inwardly he was in turmoil; outwardly he remained calm. “Mr Zhou,” he said with a grin, “why not guess?” “There is no need. The ministry certificate for a purchased appointment that you brought originally had the right surname, Yuan, but the wrong personal name. You must have borrowed it.” “Yes, yes. Nothing escapes you, Mr Zhou.” Yuan made a formal bow. “Please help me through this.” “That goes without saying. If the truth were reported, even Commander Wu would be punished for failing to detect it. There are two ways now, one easy and one troublesome. You must choose.” “Please explain them.” “The easy one first: use the name on the certificate. It is not only easy but convenient. A single official note stating that Yuan Shikai is a name adopted by Yuan So-and-so, and that you are reverting to the original name, will suffice.” Yuan did not want this easy solution. He was already well known in Korea. More importantly, everyone at court, from Empress Dowager Cixi and Prince Gong to the secretaries of the Zongli Yamen, knew that a man called Yuan Shikai had distinguished himself there. With a different name, who would recognise a mere deputy prefect?

zh: 不过他拒绝的理由，却不是这么说，『周先生，实不相瞒，』他说，『原来的部照，是我一个堂侄子的，此人业已去世，恢复原名，有许多意外的纠葛。请说难的那个办法吧！』『难的那个办法，就是你自己托人到吏部去活动。吏部那些书办，花样之多，意想不到，他们一定有办法，不过「火到猪头烂，钱到公事办」，你这件事，只怕非千金莫办。』『是、是。我照周先生的意思去办。』『好！我暂且把公事压下来，等你到吏部活动，看结果如何，再作道理。』『是。多谢、多谢。』『慰亭！』周家禄笑道∶『我有一首打油送你。』说完，拈起笔来，就桌上起公文的稿纸，一挥而就；袁世凯接过来念道∶『本是中州歪秀才，中书借得不须猜。一时大展经纶手，杀得人头七个来。』等他念完，周家禄哈哈大笑，袁世凯也只好陪着干笑几声，以示洒脱。回到自己营帐，袁世凯自然而然想起了一个人，此人名叫徐世昌，是个举人，办事很扎实，托他去活动，万无一失。只是照周家禄说，花费须一千两银子，款从何出，却费思量。
en: That, however, was not the reason he gave. “To be frank, Mr Zhou, the certificate belonged to a nephew of my clan who has died. Restoring his name could cause all sorts of unforeseen complications. Please tell me the difficult method.” “You must find someone to approach the Ministry of Personnel on your behalf. Its clerks have more tricks than one can imagine. They will certainly find a way. But ‘Keep the fire going, and the pig’s head softens; provide the money, and official business gets done.’ Your affair may cost a thousand taels.” “Yes, yes. I shall do as you advise.” “Good. I shall hold the papers back for now. Approach the ministry, and we shall decide what to do when we see the result.” “Thank you, thank you.” Zhou smiled. “Weiting, I have a bit of doggerel for you.” Taking up his brush, he wrote at one sweep on a sheet of official draft paper. Yuan read it: “A crooked Henan scholar was his start; / The borrowed secretaryship is plain. / Once he displayed his statesman’s art, / Seven severed heads became his gain.” Zhou roared with laughter. Yuan could only join in with a few dry chuckles to show how lightly he took it. Back in his tent, he naturally thought of Xu Shichang, a provincial graduate and a thoroughly reliable man. Entrusting the matter to him would ensure success. But if, as Zhou said, it would cost a thousand taels, where was the money to come from?

zh: 想来想去，只好去找张謇。他兼管着支应所，粮饷出入，大权在握，只要他点头，一千两银子就有着落了。见面招呼，一声『张先生！』张謇便是一楞，原来他称周家禄是『周先生』，叫张謇一向只『老师』二字，如今不但改了『先生』，而且还加了姓，此又何故？一时不便责问，只冷冷地答一声∶『有何见教？』袁世凯也发觉自己错了，但亦不愿再改口，只婉转地说明了自己的困难，请张謇『成全』。『成全不敢当，不过既然是朋友，理当相助。支应所的款子是公款，我不便私下借给你；如今只有一个办法，你的公费每月二百两，你写五张「领结」来，我把你的五个月公费先发给你。』『好！请问领结如何写法？』本来『印结』之结，当作承认事情已经结束来解释，辞句上不大好听，没有人去理会，只是袁世凯心里有病，将张謇所开的印结式样，拿回去一看，上面写的大意是，领到某月份公费二百两，当面点清，成色分两，均未短缺；嗣后倘有短缺，决不致提出任何补偿的要求。倒象防他会耍赖似的，心里已经不大舒服；再翻一翻一部他当作作官秘诀来用的『六部成语』，其中『吏部』有一条常用的成语，叫做『甘结』，注解是∶『凡官府断案既定，或将财物令事主领回者，均命本人作一「情甘遵命」之据，上画花押，谓这甘结』。顿时大为光火；原来所谓印结是这么一种做低服小的表示，不过画花押改为钤印而已，他觉得支应所欺人太甚了。再一想到，这回的保案中，张謇不过是以县丞保用为七品的知县；自己是同知，所谓『五品黄堂』，凭什么要向支应所具印结？当时大发了一顿牢骚，但不具印结，领不到银子，只好忍气吞声照办。可是张謇虽然听说他背后大骂『何物支应所』，觉得小人得志的那副脸嘴，令人齿冷；但还是很帮他的忙。
en: After much thought, Yuan could only turn to Zhang Jian. Zhang also managed the supply office and controlled the flow of provisions and pay. One nod from him would secure the thousand taels. Yuan greeted him with “Mr Zhang!” Zhang was taken aback. Yuan called Zhou “Mr Zhou”, but had always addressed Zhang simply as “Teacher”. Now he had changed it to “Mr”, and added the surname. Why? It was awkward to challenge him immediately, so Zhang replied coldly, “What can I do for you?” Yuan realised his mistake too, but would not correct himself. He explained his difficulty indirectly and asked Zhang to help him through it. “I would not presume to call it that. But as friends, we ought to help one another. The supply office holds public money, which I cannot lend privately. There is only one course: your official allowance is two hundred taels a month. Give me five signed acknowledgements, and I shall advance you five months.” “Good. How should I write them?” In a “sealed acknowledgement”, the word “acknowledgement” signified that a matter was concluded. The wording was not particularly pleasing, but ordinarily no one troubled about it. Yuan, however, was sensitive. When he took the form away and read it, he found it stated that he had received two hundred taels for a specified month, counted in his presence, with no deficiency in purity or weight, and that he would make no subsequent claim for compensation for any shortage. It seemed designed to prevent him from repudiating the receipt, and he was already displeased. Then he consulted the Expressions of the Six Ministries, a book he used as a guide to official life. Under Personnel was an entry for a “voluntary undertaking”: once a case was decided, or property ordered returned, the person concerned signed a document declaring willing obedience. Yuan flew into a rage. So a sealed acknowledgement was this sort of meek submission, merely replacing the signature with a seal! He felt that the supply office was treating him intolerably. Moreover, in the present recommendations Zhang had merely risen from assistant county magistrate to eligibility for a seventh-rank magistracy. Yuan was a deputy prefect, a “fifth-rank occupant of the yellow hall”. Why should he give a sealed acknowledgement to the supply office? He complained furiously, but without the documents he could not obtain the money and had to swallow his anger and comply. Zhang heard that he had been cursing behind his back—“What sort of thing is this supply office?”—and found his petty arrogance in success contemptible. Nevertheless, he continued to help him.

zh: 『慰亭，』他问，『你这银子是要在京里用？』『是的。』『那么你要寄给谁呢？』『我的一个总角之交。』袁世凯答说∶『姓徐，大概已经是新科举人了。』张謇懂他的意思，他这姓徐的朋友应北闱乡试，如今已经发榜，可能榜上有名，不过远在异国，未得京师消息，所以用了『大概』二字。『好！』张謇说道∶『我当然不能发你现银，用银票呢，又怕寄递中途失落了，也很麻烦。我有一个办法，不知道你愿意不愿意。』『喔，请张先生说。』又是『张先生』！听惯了他口口声声叫『老师』，现在第二回听见这个称呼，实在有些刺耳。不过张謇还是很耐心地说∶『本军的饷银，都是由天津「北洋公所」发的；我现在给你一张领据，你寄给你的朋友，由他直接到北洋公所去领，岂不方便。』『好，好！费心张先生了。』『你贵友的大名是哪两个字？』张謇又说∶『领据上指明由某人去领，比较保险。』袁世凯觉得这话也不错，点点头说∶『叫徐世昌。五世其昌的世昌。』『哪里人？』『这也要写在领据上？』『不是这意思。我要写明他的身份，赴北闱当然不是监生，就是生员，生员就要写明哪一县的生员，所以我问他是哪里人。『他是生员。』袁世凯说∶『他原来浙江宁波人，乾隆年间迁居天津，他高祖是河南南阳知县，殁在任上，葬在河南汲县，他家以后就一直寄居在那里，所以他又算浙江人，也算直隶人，或者河南人。』『这样说，他还是天津的生员，如果是汲县进的学，就得在河南乡试。』
en: “Weiting, is this money to be used in Beijing?” “Yes.” “To whom will you send it?” “A childhood friend named Xu. By now he is probably a newly successful provincial graduate.” Zhang understood. His friend had sat the northern provincial examination, whose results were now out. He might have passed, but Yuan, far away in another country, had not received the news; hence “probably”. “Very well,” Zhang said. “I cannot give you silver to send, of course. A banknote might be lost in the post, which would cause trouble. I have a method, if you agree.” “Please explain, Mr Zhang.” “Mr Zhang” again! After hearing “Teacher” so often, this second use jarred. Still, Zhang patiently continued. “Our army’s pay is issued through the Beiyang Office in Tianjin. I shall give you an order to collect the money. Send it to your friend, and he can draw it there directly. Would that not be convenient?” “Excellent. Thank you for your trouble, Mr Zhang.” “What is your friend’s personal name? It will be safer to name the person authorised to collect it.” Yuan agreed. “Xu Shichang. The characters for shichang come from ‘May his descendants prosper for five generations’.” “Where is he from?” “Must that go on the order too?” “Not for its own sake. I must specify his status. To sit the northern provincial examination, he must be either an Imperial Academy student or a county licentiate. If the latter, I must state the county. That is why I ask.” “He is a licentiate. His family originally came from Ningbo in Zhejiang and moved to Tianjin in the Qianlong reign. His great-great-grandfather served as magistrate of Nanyang in Henan, died in office and was buried in Ji county. The family has lived there since. So he can be considered a Zhejiang man, a Zhili man or a Henan man.” “Then his licentiate registration must still be in Tianjin. If he had qualified in Ji county, he would have had to sit the Henan examination.”

zh: 张謇开了领据，指明由『原天津生员徐世昌』具领『。等这张邻据寄寄到徐世昌手里，他已经是新科举人了。徐世昌是与他的胞弟徐世光一起下科场的。三场考毕，在等候发榜的那一个月之中，功名心热，得失这念梗在胸中，有些食不甘味、寝不安枕；常常往来的一个好朋友，便劝他去求一支签。他这个朋友叫柯绍半，字凤笙，山东胶州人。告诉徐世昌说∶『琉璃厂的吕祖祠，那里的签，最灵验不过，有求必应；有应必中。你何妨去求一求看。』徐世昌欣然乐从，到了琉璃厂吕祖祠，看香火比它西面的火神庙还盛，信心便又添了几分。当下虏诚祷祝，抽了一支签出来，上面写的一首诗是∶『八九玄功已有基，频添火候莫差池，待看十二重楼透，便是丹成鹤到时。』『这好象工夫还不到。』徐世昌说∶『今科恐怕无望。』『不然。』柯绍半说∶『照我看，这是指春闱而言，第二句「频添火候莫差池」，是说你秋闱得意以后，要加紧用功，多写写「大卷子」，明年会试中式，殿试得鼎甲，那岂非「十二重楼诱」出？』徐世昌听这一解，大为高兴。再看诗后的『断曰』∶『光前裕后，昌大其门庭』，益发满心欢悦了。
en: Zhang issued the order, naming “Xu Shichang, formerly a licentiate of Tianjin” as the recipient. By the time it reached Xu, he had indeed become a provincial graduate. He and his younger brother Xu Shiguang had taken the examination together. After its three sessions, during the month’s wait for the results, his eagerness for a degree and anxiety over success or failure robbed his food of flavour and his sleep of ease. A close friend advised him to seek a divination lot. The friend was Ke Shaoban, courtesy name Fengsheng, from Jiaozhou in Shandong. “The lots at the shrine of Immortal Lü in Liulichang are extraordinarily accurate,” he said. “Every question receives an answer, and every answer proves true. Why not try?” Xu readily agreed. At the shrine he found the worship even more fervent than at the Fire God Temple to its west, which strengthened his faith. He prayed sincerely and drew a lot bearing this verse: “The mystic work has laid its base; / Feed the fire well, make no mistake. / When twelvefold towers yield their inner space, / The elixir forms, and cranes awake.” “It seems my work is not yet complete,” Xu said. “Perhaps there is no hope in this examination.” “Not so,” Ke replied. “I think it refers to the spring examination. The second line, ‘Feed the fire well, make no mistake’, means that after success in the autumn, you must study harder and practise more full examination papers. Next year you will pass the metropolitan examination and gain one of the top three places in the palace examination. Would that not be breaking through the ‘twelvefold towers’?” Xu was delighted by this interpretation. Then he read the pronouncement beneath the poem: “Bring glory to those before and abundance to those after; make the family flourish greatly.” His happiness increased still further.

zh: 到得登榜那天，由半夜等到天亮，由天亮等到日中，捷报来了，不过徐世昌却格外难堪，原来他的胞弟徐世光中了第九十五名举人。当下开发了喜封，在会馆中乱过一阵，等静下来不由得凄然下泪。『大哥，我看你的闱墨比我强。』徐世光安慰他说∶『一定是五经魁，报来还早呢！』原来乡试发榜，弥封卷子拆一名，写一名，从前一天半夜，一直要写到第二天晚上。向例写榜从第六名开始，前五名称为，『五经魁』，留到最后揭晓，那时已是第二天晚上，到拆五经魁的卷子时，闱中仆役杂工，人手一支红蜡烛，光耀如白昼，称为『闹榜』。其时黄昏未到，所以徐世光说是『报来还早呢』。『报！』外面又热闹了，徐世昌侧耳静听，报的是∶『贵府徐大少爷郎世昌，高中壬午科顺天乡试第一百四十五名举人。』这是真的吗？当然是真的，泥金报条上所写的，还怕会眼花看错，报子『连三元』来讨赏，赏了二十两还不肯，说是∶『大少爷、二少爷，双喜临门，起码得赏个一百两银子。』这总不是假的吧！争多论少，终于以四十两银子打发了『连三元』。不过这是『头报』，接下来还有『二报』、『三报』，少不得还要破费几两银子。这一夜会馆中很热闹，徐氏兄弟棠棣联辉，他们所住的那个院子，更是贺客接踵不断，直到午夜过后，才得清静下来，虽然人已经非常困倦了，但徐世昌的精神亢奋，一点睡意都没有。
en: On the day the list appeared, he waited from midnight until dawn and from dawn until noon. At last a messenger arrived with good news—but it left Xu Shichang acutely embarrassed. His younger brother, Xu Shiguang, had passed in ninety-fifth place. Rewards were paid and the provincial hostel bustled for a while. Once it grew quiet, Shichang could not help shedding miserable tears. “Elder Brother, I thought your examination essays better than mine,” Shiguang consoled him. “You must be among the top five. It is too early for that news.” When the provincial results were posted, the sealed names were opened and written out one by one, a process lasting from the previous midnight until the following evening. By custom, the list began with sixth place. The top five, the “Leaders of the Five Classics”, were disclosed last, by which time it was evening. When those scripts were opened, every servant and labourer in the examination compound held a red candle, making the place bright as day. This was called “making a stir over the list”. Dusk had not yet come, which was why Shiguang said the news was still to arrive. “News!” There was another commotion outside. Shichang listened intently. “Your household’s eldest young master, Xu Shichang, has passed the Shuntian provincial examination of the Renwu year in one hundred and forty-fifth place!” Could it be true? Of course it was. He might misread the gold-printed announcement, but the messenger, nicknamed “Three Firsts in Succession”, was demanding his reward. Even twenty taels did not satisfy him. “The eldest young master and the second young master—double happiness at your door! At least a hundred taels is called for.” Surely this could not be false. After bargaining, they finally sent him away with forty. That was only the first announcement; second and third messengers followed, costing a few more taels. The hostel was lively that night. With both Xu brothers bringing honour to the family, congratulations flowed especially thickly into their courtyard. Not until after midnight was it quiet. Though physically exhausted, Shichang was too excited to feel sleepy.

zh: 『二弟，好灵啊！』徐世昌突然跳起来，大声嚷着，倒把徐世光吓一大跳。『大哥，什么东西好灵？』『，二弟，你不能用「东西」这种字眼，我是说吕祖的签好灵。你看。』徐世昌指着签词∶『「光前裕后」，不明明道破，你的名次在前吗？』『呃！』徐世光也觉得有点道理，『真的，吕祖已经明示，我要沾大哥的光。』『不过，二弟，你也别太得意。你将来的成就不及我。』他以兄长的身份，用这样的口吻说话，徐世光自然只有保持沉默。『怎么，徐世昌说∶』你不相信？『『不是我不相信。我将来的成就不及大哥，也是可想而知的；不过刚刚是在谈吕祖的签，大哥一定在签上有所领悟，而没有说出一个究竟来，我就不便置喙了。』『当然！当然是签上透露的玄机，你看∶』昌大其门庭「，不就是我徐世昌才能荣宗耀祖吗？『『徐世光无话可答，只有连声应说是。『只有大哥才能昌大咱们徐家的门庭。』『二弟，』徐世昌神情肃穆地说∶『明天到吕祖祠去磕个头，一则谢谢他老人家的指点；再则今后的行止，也要请他老人家指点。』徐世光听兄长的话，第二天又一起到吕祖祠祝告求签。这回是各求一支，叩问行止，徐世光求得的签，意思不是如回家读书，明年春天会试再来；徐世昌的那一支是∶『出门何所图，胜如家里坐，虽无上天梯，一步高一步。』『二弟，你回去，我不能回去。』徐世昌说∶『签上说得很明白，出门胜似在家。我在京用功为妙。』
en: “Younger Brother, how accurate it was!” Shichang suddenly sprang up and shouted, giving Shiguang a fright. “What thing was accurate?” “You must not call it a ‘thing’. I mean Immortal Lü’s lot. Look!” He pointed to the words. “‘Glory to those before’—Guang, glory, plainly says that you would rank before me!” “Ah!” Shiguang thought there was something in it. “True. The Immortal indicated that I would share in Elder Brother’s glory.” “But do not be too pleased with yourself. Your future achievements will not equal mine.” As the elder brother spoke in that tone, Shiguang could only remain silent. “What? Do you not believe me?” “It is not that. One can readily imagine that my achievements will be less than yours. But we were discussing the lot. You must have found some meaning in it. Until you explained, it was not for me to speak.” “Of course! It reveals the secret. Look: ‘Make the family flourish greatly.’ Chang, flourish—that means I, Xu Shichang, will bring glory to our ancestors.” Shiguang had no answer beyond repeated agreement. “Only Elder Brother can make our Xu family flourish.” Shichang grew solemn. “Tomorrow we shall bow at the shrine: first to thank the Immortal for his guidance, and then to ask his advice on our next steps.” Shiguang obeyed. The next day they returned and each drew a lot about what to do. Shiguang’s advised him to return home to study and come again for the metropolitan examination in spring. Shichang’s read: “What gain in going from your door? / More than in sitting home once more. / Though no stair reaches Heaven’s height, / Each step will raise you towards the light.” “You go home, Younger Brother. I cannot. The lot is clear: going out is better than staying home. I should study in Beijing.”

zh: 徐世光自是听他作主，一个人先回家乡；徐世昌却寻得一个馆地，是兵部尚书张之万家，他们是世交，张之万将他请了去陪他的儿子张瑞荫一起读书，附带办办笔墨，住在张家后院。后院很宽敞，徐世昌布置了卧室、书房以外，还有余屋，打算着设一个神龛，供奉吕祖；主意将定未定之际，夜得一梦，梦见吕祖，告诉他说∶『你果真有心供奉我的香火，事须秘密；我云游稍倦，需要小憩时，自会降临，把你这里作为一个避嚣的静室，不宜有人打搅。』平时做梦，刚醒来时还记得，稍停一停，便忘得精光；只有这个梦，在他第二天起身漱洗时，还清清楚楚地记得。徐世昌认为吕祖托梦，非同小可，不过一定得遵照神灵指示办事，所以一切亲自动手，找一间最隐密的房间，悄悄置了一座神龛；白天门户紧闭，晚上直到院门关紧闩住，方开密室，在神前烧香膜拜，同时置了一副『吕祖神签』，以便疑难不决时，得以请吕祖指点。
en: Shiguang naturally accepted his decision and went home alone. Shichang found a tutoring place in the household of Zhang Zhiwan, Minister of War. The two families were old friends. Zhang invited him to study alongside his son, Zhang Ruiyin, and help with correspondence, lodging him in the rear courtyard. It was spacious. After setting up a bedroom and study, Xu still had rooms to spare and considered installing a shrine to Immortal Lü. Before he had quite decided, he dreamed that the Immortal said, “If you truly wish to offer me incense, you must keep it secret. When my wanderings tire me and I need a brief rest, I shall come and use your place as a quiet retreat from the world. I must not be disturbed.” Usually he remembered a dream upon waking, then soon forgot it entirely. This one remained perfectly clear even as he washed the next morning. He regarded such a visitation as momentous and was determined to follow the divine instructions. Doing everything himself, he chose the most secluded room and quietly installed a shrine. Its door stayed shut all day. At night, only after the courtyard gate had been closed and bolted would he open the secret room, burn incense and worship. He also obtained a set of “Immortal Lü’s Divination Lots”, so that he could seek guidance whenever in doubt.

zh: 这天接到袁世凯的来信，少不得也要求支签，问一问这件事能不能办？签上指示，不但可办，而且要速办；迟则不及。当下便向张瑞荫打听，吏部有没有熟人？『什么事？』『是一个朋友袁慰亭，有点麻烦。』徐世昌细说了缘由。『这是吏部文选句该管。』张瑞荫说∶『这种事找司官，不如找书办。』『正是，袁慰亭信中关照，也是要找书办；我问有没有熟人，就是说吏部书办之中有没有够交情的？』『我们这种人家，怎么会跟胥吏有交情？』张瑞荫说∶『等我来问问门上老牛。』徐世昌知道失言了，脸一红说∶『是，是，我说错了。就拜托你找老牛问一问吧？』
en: When Yuan’s letter arrived, he naturally drew a lot to ask whether the matter could be managed. The answer was not only yes, but that he must act quickly: delay would make him too late. He immediately asked Zhang Ruiyin whether he knew anyone at the Ministry of Personnel. “What is the matter?” “A friend, Yuan Weiting, has a difficulty.” Xu explained it in detail. “That belongs to the ministry’s Civil Appointments Department,” Zhang said. “For such business, a clerk is more useful than an officer.” “Exactly. Yuan stressed the same thing in his letter. When I asked whether you knew anyone, I meant whether you had a sufficiently friendly connection among the clerks.” “How could a family such as ours be on friendly terms with petty clerks? Let me ask Old Niu at the gate.” Realising his blunder, Xu blushed. “Yes, yes. I misspoke. Please ask Old Niu for me.”

zh: 将老牛找了来一问，他说∶『我们熟识一个姓何的，在吏部文选人司很吃得开。不过不知道在在京？』『怎么？吏部的书办不在京里会在什么地方呢？』『老何原籍山西蒲州，前一阵子我听说他要请假回老家去上坟，不知道走了没有？』『你赶快去一趟。』张瑞荫说∶『看看何书办在不在？在呢，就跟他说，有这么一件事。』这件事的始末，由徐世昌告诉了老牛，请老牛去谈。这是有回扣的事，老牛很巴结地，当时便去找何书办接头。到晚来回话，『好险！』老牛说道∶『只差一步，行李都上车了，明儿一大早就走。』『喔，你跟他谈了？』『是的。』『有办法没有？』『他们怎么会没办法？』老牛笑道∶『就怕「盘子」谈不拢。』『他开的「盘口」是多少？』张瑞荫问。
en: They summoned the gatekeeper. “We know a man called He,” he said. “He has considerable influence in Civil Appointments. But I do not know whether he is in Beijing.” “Why? Where else would a ministry clerk be?” “Old He comes from Puzhou in Shanxi. Some time ago I heard he intended to take leave and visit his ancestral graves. I do not know whether he has gone.” “Go there at once,” Zhang Ruiyin said. “Find out whether he is still here. If he is, tell him about the matter.” Xu explained everything to Old Niu and asked him to negotiate. There was a commission to be earned, so the gatekeeper eagerly went straight to Clerk He. That evening he returned. “A close thing! One step later and we would have missed him. His luggage was already on the cart, and he leaves first thing tomorrow.” “Oh? Did you speak to him?” “Yes.” “Is there a solution?” “How could they lack solutions?” Old Niu laughed. “The only question is whether we can agree on the price.” “What price has he named?” Zhang asked.
